summary: Audited the journal's id/filename handling against the real 450-segment journal, verified all legacy segments remain readable with no id collisions, and added a regression test that seeds a legacy bare-ordinal segment alongside a new suffixed one to lock in the mixed-format contract. Then proposed three next improvements: retire the orphaned .agent-journal/ directory, fix segment boundaries, and build a digest layer.
decisions: No migration is performed for legacy bare-ordinal ids like '0310'; ids are only ever string-compared and concatenated into filenames, so legacy and new formats coexist without rewriting.
Bare ordinal ids and suffixed ids are distinct index keys and distinct filenames, so they cannot collide and shadowing is impossible.

A new regression test in journal-store.test.ts seeds a legacy segment directly on disk (old filename + old index line) and asserts reads, appends, and list behavior over the mixed set, instead of relying on the read-only assertion that nothing parses ids numerically.
errors: First verification script /tmp/verify.ts failed under tsx because top-level await is not supported with the 'cjs' output format; resolved by renaming to .mts and rerunning as ESM.
